urn:eigenius:core:description: A class represents an ontological type. Classes declare which properties their instances must or should provide. Class is an instance of itself.

Catch-all class for entities whose more specific class isn't asserted. Used by importers and other tooling for instances that need to participate in pattern matching without a domain-specific Class declaration — OBO `INDIVIDUAL` nodes, anonymous edge targets that no `nodes[]` entry covered, etc. Resource sits at the top of the class lattice as the universal supertype.
A property defines a named attribute that resources may carry. Properties declare their data_type and optional constraints (format, pattern, content type, class types).
A data type defines a primitive value type that determines the JSON-level representation of property values.
A format defines a validation constraint on string values. Formats are checked by the kernel during validation.
An encoding declares how binary content is represented within a string value.
A conditional requirement that makes properties required or recommended based on the value of another property.
Declares class membership. A resource's is_a is an array of classes it is an instance of.
Human-readable description of a resource.
Short identifier for a resource, used by external integrations. Must be unique within a class's effective property set.
Parent classes in the inheritance hierarchy. A subclass inherits requires and recommends from all ancestors.
Properties that instances of this class must provide.
Properties that instances of this class should provide.
The primitive data_type constraining a property's values. Determines the JSON-level representation.
A named format constraint for string values. The kernel validates string values against the declared format.
A regular expression constraint for string values. The value must fully match the pattern (ECMA 262 syntax).
MIME type declaring the format of content embedded in a string value (e.g., text/markdown, text/html, image/png).
Encoding used for binary content embedded in a string value.
The data_type of elements in a value_array property.

Allowed types for resource, resource_array, or inductive property values. Each listed IRI is either a `core:Class` (the value is a ResourceRef/Embedded whose `is_a` must match — possibly transitively via `subclass_of`) or a `core:InductiveType` (the value is a `Value::Json` tagged-dict tree `{ "ctor": ..., "args": [...] }` validated against the type's ctors and arg_types). When the entry is an InductiveType the list must hold exactly one IRI — inductive values are uniquely typed (D32 §3.5). For `data_type: core:resource(_array)` either form is admissible; for `data_type: core:inductive` only the singleton InductiveType form is admissible.
Restricts which class types this property may be used on. If omitted, the property may be used on any resource.
Restricts resource or resource_array property values to a specific set of resources (by IRI identity).
Minimum value (inclusive) for integer or float property values.
Maximum value (inclusive) for integer or float property values.
Minimum length for string values (in characters) or array properties (in elements).
Maximum length for string values (in characters) or array properties (in elements).
Conditional requirements on a class. An array of ConditionalRequirement resources that make properties required or recommended based on the value of another property.
The property whose value triggers the conditional requirement.
The condition matches if the property's value is any of the listed values.
Properties that become required when the condition matches.
Properties that become recommended when the condition matches.
Optional fetchable IRL where the resource can be found or was sourced from.

Boolean flag indicating the resource is deprecated by its source authority. Set by importers when the upstream record carried a deprecation marker (OBO `meta.deprecated`, OWL `owl:deprecated`); the resource itself stays in the document for back-reference but downstream consumers can filter it out via a `WHERE NOT ?x.deprecated = true` style guard.
UTF-8 string. May carry format, content_type, and/or content_encoding constraints via the property definition.
Signed integer in the 53-bit safe range (-(2^53-1) to 2^53-1). Represented as a JSON number with no decimal point.
64-bit IEEE 754 floating-point number. Represented as a JSON number.
Boolean true/false value.
A reference to another resource (IRI string) or an embedded resource (nested object without @id).
An ordered array of resource references (IRI strings) and/or embedded resources (nested objects).
An ordered array of homogeneous primitive values. The element type is declared via the element_type property.
An opaque JSON value. Not validated by the ontology.

A typed inductive value — a tagged dict `{ "ctor": <ctor_name>, "args": [<arg_value>, ...] }` whose ctor is declared on a referenced InductiveType. The property's `class_types` must contain exactly one InductiveType IRI (D32 §3.5); the validator walks the value tree against the InductiveType's ctors and arg_types at commit time. The wire shape is opaque JSON to surrounding chain queries; institutions decode it into their target language for evaluation.
A prompt template string with {{property_iri}} substitution patterns. The template's property references form a dependent type that determines input requirements.
Base64 encoding for binary data embedded in a string value.
ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD).
ISO 8601 date-time with timezone (e.g., 2026-04-11T14:30:00Z).
A valid IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier, RFC 3987).
A UUID (RFC 4122).
A valid regular expression (ECMA 262 syntax).
A coinductive type defined by its observations (D11). Dual of Class: Class defines a type by constructors and fields; CodataType defines it by the observations that can be made on its values.
A single observation declaration on a CodataType: a name and a result type.
Ordered list of Observation resources declared by a CodataType.
The local name of an observation (e.g. 'head', 'tail').
Result type of an observation: a reference to a Class, CodataType, or DataType resource resolved via the layer chain.

An inductive type defined by its constructors (D19, Phase 11b). Dual of CodataType: an inductive type is built up from a finite set of constructors, while a codata type is taken apart by its observations.
A single constructor of an InductiveType: a name and an ordered list of argument types. The constructor's result type is the inductive itself applied to its parameters.

A constructor-argument type: a parameterised name reference. `type_name` is either a class IRI (Nat, ex:Foo) or a bare parameter name from the enclosing inductive's type parameters (e.g. `A` in List(A)). `type_args` carries the parameters when the reference itself is parametric (e.g. `List(A)`). `arg_name` is an optional readable slot name used by JSON-authored ontologies and mirror generators.
A type parameter on an InductiveType: a name and a kind. Phase 11b admits only kind `Set`; the kind field is kept so future extensions can declare higher-universe parameters without a schema break.

The class of macro-definition resources — the chain-resident form of an ESL `macro` declaration (its AST is stored on `core:macro_decl_json`). Macros expand at compile time and emit no chain resources of their own; this class is the type their definition resources are instances of, so `is_a core:Macro` resolves like any other type reference.
Ordered list of constructor declarations on an InductiveType.
The result sort an InductiveType's constructors produce (e.g. `Prop`, `Set`). A string naming the sort.
Index arguments of an indexed inductive family (D48) — the per-index parameter declarations distinguishing an indexed family from a parametric type. Each element is an embedded InductiveParam.
The encoded type expression (eigentt) of a constructor — the full arrow type a constructor inhabits. Carried as the tagged-dict JSON encoding the kernel decoder parses back.
The JSON-encoded macro declaration (parameters + expansion) carried by a core:Macro resource; the ESL compiler decodes it back into a MacroDecl at compile time.
Ordered list of type parameters on an InductiveType or CodataType. Empty for non-parametric types (Nat, Bool, non-sized streams).

The local name of a constructor — the unqualified ctor-name string keyed into the parent inductive's ctor set. Carried by `InductiveCtor` declarations (which `require` it) and reused by higher-layer inductive-value resources (e.g. the institution layer's kernel-emitted `Verdict`, carrying `Holds` / `Fails` / `Undecidable`). No `domain` whitelist: applicability is declared class-side via `requires`, and a property-side whitelist could not span the core/institution layer boundary without an upward reference — the reuse across layers is intentional.
Ordered list of constructor argument types. Empty for nullary constructors.
Either a class IRI or a bare parameter name from the enclosing inductive's type parameters.

Optional readable name for an InductiveArgType slot (e.g. `head`, `tail`, `name`, `body`). Mirror generators use it for typed-language struct field names; chain readers use it for diagnostics. ESL-compiled inductives may omit it (the compiler carries the source-position pattern through other channels). Recommended-not-required so existing ESL-emitted ctors continue to validate.
Type arguments applied to a parametric type reference, e.g. `[A]` for `List(A)`. Empty for bare references.
The local name of an InductiveParam.
The kind of an InductiveParam — currently always `urn:eigenius:core:Set`.

Atomic propositional assertion: `Asserts(iri) : Prop` carries no inhabitants of its own — the type has zero constructors — so different IRIs produce distinct propositions whose only inhabitation paths are institutional dispatch (typically Lean producing a proof term the in-kernel checker validates) or introduction as an `eigentt:Axiom`. The uniform-parameter shape — `iri` as a parameter, not an index — keeps the declaration trivial; with D48 indexed families now landed an alternative `Asserts : core:iri -> Prop` indexed encoding is expressible but not used here, since the parameter shape is the cleaner default. The witness emitter for `DeclarationTrace` / `ObservationTrace` / `ProgramTrace` resources uses `Asserts(target_iri)` as the default canonical proposition when the target carries no explicit `reflection:canonical_proposition`. The witness-emitter integration of that default is staged with D39's `JustifiedBy` consumer-site work so both sides agree on the iri-argument encoding.

The standard option/maybe parametric inductive: a value of `Option(A)` is either `none` or `some(value: A)`. Mirrors the canonical kernel-side declaration at `crate::nbe::term::option_decl`. Used by `MergeComorphism` to type the optional ancestor argument of a `(A, A, Option<A>) -> A` witness signature. Separate from the anonymous `Sum(some A | none 1)` encoding the type checker uses for recommended properties (`prop?` lowering) — that encoding is internal; this declaration is the named, chain-visible type for use sites that need to refer to `Option` by IRI.

A typed witness for a `Witness`-strategy merge resolution (D20 §6.1). Carries a `merge_transformation` whose Component must have signature `(A, A, Option<A>) -> A` where A is the class of the IRI being merged: the two branch values and the optional ancestor value collapse into the merged value. The class A is pinned by `merge_target_class` so the witness can be early-rejected at apply time when used against a mismatched conflict (D37 §6.2). Distinct from the institution-layer `Comorphism` (which witnesses cross-institution translation); the two share the typing-discipline framing but live at different layers because merge resolution is a core concern while institution boundaries are not.

Reference to the EigenTT term (typed expression) realising the merge witness. The kernel verifies at resolution-submission time (D20 §6.1) that the term's type equals `(A, A, Option<A>) -> A` for the class A of the IRI being resolved — branch_a value, branch_b value, optional ancestor value, merged value. No `class_types` narrowing here because the core ontology loads before `program`, so the EigenTT expression classes aren't yet in the chain at validation time. The kernel's resolution-submission signature check is what actually enforces the typing discipline; this property's `data_type: resource` keeps the structural shape minimal.

The class A a `MergeComorphism` is declared for (D37 §3.3, §6.1). Pinned at commit time so the witness can be early-rejected when applied to a mismatched conflict class, and so the notebook's WitnessEditor can show only applicable comorphisms for the current conflict's class. Required on every `MergeComorphism`. The property's value is the IRI of a `Class` resource committed earlier in the chain.

Chain-resident audit record of how a single conflict was resolved inside a merge layer (D38 §3). Committed alongside the resolved bodies by `commit_resolutions_as_merge_layer`, one record per conflict, so the merge layer's reasoning becomes inspectable through ordinary EigenQL queries without re-running the classifier. Required slots pin the strategy + conflict id; per-strategy optional slots capture the strategy's specific choices (witness IRI, rename direction, quotient kind, restructure parent). Synthesised `@id` uses content-hash form `urn:eigenius:auto:merge-record:<sha256>` so deterministic resolutions of the same conflict produce the same record IRI across runs.

The classifier-emitted conflict id (D38 §3.1). Opaque-string shape matching `ConflictId`'s wire form (e.g., `iri_collision:urn:project:patient_42`) so a reader can correlate the record with a fresh `PreviewCascade` run against an earlier chain state.

Name of the resolution strategy applied. One of `Witness`, `Rename`, `SchemaQuotient`, `Restructure` — mirroring the `MergeResolution` enum variants. Per-strategy detail lives in the optional `merge_record_*` slots; the strategy name lets a reader pre-filter without inspecting the full record body.
Hex layer id of the layer that contributed branch A's body at the conflict IRI. Absent when the conflict shape has no single-IRI per-branch body (e.g., cycle-shaped conflicts).
Hex layer id of the layer that contributed branch B's body at the conflict IRI. Absent for cycle-shaped conflicts.
Hex layer id of the ancestor's body at the conflict IRI. Absent for IRIs that didn't exist at the LCA (one-sided additions).

Set for `Witness` strategy: IRI of the `MergeComorphism` that was applied. The comorphism resource is copied into the same merge layer (D38 §3.2) so the IRI always resolves on the merge layer's own chain regardless of GC of the source branch.
Hex layer id of the layer the witness was originally committed on, before the copy into the merge layer (D38 §3.2). Preserves the authoring-time attribution for audit purposes.
Set for `Rename` strategy: `a` or `b`, identifying which side of the merge span the rename was applied to.
Set for `Rename` strategy: IRI being renamed away from on the renamed side.
Set for `Rename` strategy: new IRI the renamed-side resource is committed under in the merge layer.
Set for `SchemaQuotient` strategy: one of `KeepBoth`, `KeepOne`, `KeepNeither` — the quotient flavour applied.
Set for `SchemaQuotient` strategy with `KeepOne` quotient kind: `a` or `b`, identifying the surviving side.
Set for `Restructure` strategy: IRI of the introduced common parent class.
Set for `Restructure` strategy: IRI of the class whose contradictory `subclass_of` arrows motivated the restructure.

Declares that a target Property's values should be inverted-indexed for chain-aware BM25 retrieval (D43 §3.1). First-class Resource separate from the Property it targets so indexing decisions don't modify the data-model identity; per-deployment indexing of shared schemas; index lifecycle independent of Property lifecycle. Segments are keyed by the TextIndex IRI (not the target Property IRI) so divergent indexing configurations across branches stay storage-safe. v1 multiplicity constraint: at most one active (non-shadowed) TextIndex per target Property per chain head.

Declares that a target Property's values should be embedded under a named model and stored for chain-aware vector retrieval (D43 §3.1). First-class Resource separate from the Property it targets; segments are keyed by the VectorIndex IRI so model/strategy changes across branches stay storage-safe. v1 multiplicity constraint: at most one active (non-shadowed) VectorIndex per target Property per chain head. Updating any parameter that affects segment contents (model, dimensionality, distance, HNSW parameters) requires atomic reindex (D43 §5.7), mechanically expressed as a fresh VectorIndex Resource with a new IRI shadowing the prior one.

Declares that a target Property's values should be EXACT-indexed for chain-aware `value -> subjects` lookup (D65). The third declared index kind alongside TextIndex (BM25, fuzzy) and VectorIndex (dense, fuzzy); ValueIndex is exact and normalized — the right tool for keyed lookup of a string/literal property (a lexical form, a gene symbol, an accession) where the triple index does not apply (it indexes only IRI-valued properties) and BM25 is wrong (tokenised + ranked). First-class Resource separate from the Property it targets so indexing decisions don't modify the data-model identity; index lifecycle independent of Property lifecycle. Entries are keyed by the ValueIndex IRI (not the target Property IRI) so divergent indexing configurations across branches stay storage-safe. v1 multiplicity constraint: at most one active (non-shadowed) ValueIndex per target Property per chain head.

The Property an Index Resource targets for indexing. The value is the IRI of a Property resource resolved through the visible chain at Load time. Shared by TextIndex, VectorIndex, and ValueIndex (an Index Resource of any kind references its target Property via this slot).

Names the normalization a ValueIndex applies to a property value before keying it for EXACT lookup. Unlike a text analyzer it NORMALIZES, never tokenizes — the value is kept whole (multiword forms stay a single key). A fixed, closed enum (each corresponds to a normalization function in the kernel), so the `value_normalizer` slot is `allows_only`-narrowed to these instances. v1 ships `identity`, `lowercase`, `lowercase_trim`.
No normalization — the value is keyed verbatim (byte-exact).
Unicode lowercase. Case-insensitive exact lookup (e.g. the lexicon's `form` index: `BRCA1` and `brca1` key alike).
Unicode lowercase plus trimming of surrounding whitespace.

The normalization a ValueIndex applies to property values (and to the query key) before exact lookup. Fixed enum — see `core:ValueNormalizer`. Default `urn:eigenius:core:normalizers:identity` when omitted.

Names the analyzer that tokenises, lowercases, and stems property values for inverted indexing. v1 ships `en-stem-v1` (Unicode segmentation + lowercase + Porter English stem) and `en-no-stem` (Unicode segmentation + lowercase only). Additional analyzers are additive — registered analyzer IDs are validated at query time against the registry rather than at schema time, so no `allows_only` narrowing here. The analyzer ID is recorded in each segment's `text_stats` so the query-side analyzer matches the index-side analyzer.

IRI of the Embedder Component (D43 §5.2) whose output dimensionality this index commits to. The kernel verifies at parse time that the IRI references a registered Embedder Component. No `class_types` narrowing here because Component definitions don't live in the core ontology (matching the merge_transformation pattern); validation happens at the Component registry, not at schema load.

Declared output dimensionality of the embedder model. Statically declared on the VectorIndex Resource so EigenQL can type vector expressions at parse time without runtime probes. Must match the Embedder Component's declared output dimensionality (verified at parse).

Names a distance metric used by the vector retrieval kernel. Each registered metric corresponds to a SIMD distance kernel in the kernel implementation. Instances of this class are loaded by the core ontology; v1 ships `cosine`, `l2`, `dot`.
Cosine similarity, mapped to a distance via `1 - cos(theta)`. Bounded in [0, 2] for unit vectors. The default for embedding workloads where vector magnitudes are not semantically meaningful.
Euclidean (L2) distance. Appropriate when vector magnitudes carry signal.
Negative dot product (so larger means closer for consistent top-k ordering). Used when the embedder produces vectors whose dot product is calibrated to similarity.

Distance metric used at index time (segment encoding) and at query time (VECTOR_NEAR / VECTOR_SIM). Fixed per VectorIndex; not overridable per call in v1. Default `urn:eigenius:core:distances:cosine` when omitted.

Names a per-segment search strategy. Each instance maps to a code path in the vector-index reader/writer. v1 ships `flat`, `hnsw`, `auto`; v2 extensions (IVF, quantisation) will land as additional instances without breaking the property's domain.
Always brute-force k-NN over the per-segment vector array. Exact results. Best for segments under ~50K vectors.
Always HNSW (approximate nearest neighbour). Best for large segments (≥100K vectors). Returns approximate results with a configurable recall/cost tradeoff via `ef`.
Build HNSW when a segment's vector count exceeds a configurable threshold (default ~50K), brute-force below it. The default for most workloads.
Per-segment search strategy for a VectorIndex. Default `urn:eigenius:core:strategies:auto` when omitted.

HNSW graph parameter: maximum number of connections per node per level. Higher M improves recall at the cost of build time and graph storage. Default 16 when omitted. Required to be consistent across all segments of a given VectorIndex (changing it requires the §5.7 atomic-reindex policy).

HNSW build-time exploration depth. Higher values improve graph quality (and therefore query-time recall at a given `ef`) at the cost of build time. Default 200 when omitted. Required to be consistent across all segments of a given VectorIndex.

Controls when the post-Load embedding sweep runs for a VectorIndex. v1 ships `eager_on_load` as the only implemented instance; `lazy_on_query` and `manual` are reserved instances for future revisions.
The embedding sweep runs immediately after Layer commit, materialising vec_seg entries for the new content. v1 default.
Reserved for a future revision. Embedding deferred until query time, with per-resource materialisation on first access.
Reserved for a future revision. Embedding triggered only by explicit user action; useful for offline indexing workflows.
Controls when the post-Load embedding sweep runs for this VectorIndex. Default `urn:eigenius:core:embedding_policies:eager_on_load` when omitted.

BM25 text index over `core:description` — makes every resource's natural-language description searchable chain-wide (D43 §3.1). Declared here, with the property it targets, because `core:description` is a universal core property (any resource may carry a description); an index is per-property, so its home is the ontology that owns the property, not a domain layer. This is the retrieval accelerator ONLY — which hits are eligible grounding targets (a domain concept vs an arbitrary meta-class or a predicate Axiom) is a resolver-side decision (an `is_a`/lattice filter over the triple index), never encoded in the index. Its primary consumer is D63 lexicon-augmentation §6a index c (concept-gloss OOV grounding: noun-class/instance glosses and verb/adjective Axiom glosses), but every description-bearing resource is indexed. One active TextIndex per target Property per chain head.
